notes: After two early steals the Runner clicked for credits every turn from T10 to T16, hoarding 28 credits with 5 cards in grip and never installing or running, while the Corp advanced and scored four agendas in Server 1. On T12 it reached N-Pot with 10 credits and let it end the run without breaking it, even though Sang Kancil had broken it before.

Good start (two HQ steals), but the economy then ran dry and the Runner kept making half-funded runs: it pumped Utae and Rising Tide partway without breaking, lost cards to net damage, and once broke Karuna and then jacked out. Repeated HQ runs kept seeing La Costa Grid while remote agendas were scored.

It never installed a single card all game, then clicked for credits for ten turns up to 41 credits while the Corp scored repeatedly out of a one-ice remote. Its only remote runs facechecked Tree Line and Akhet with no breaker.
Fast, sensible aggression: Bravado on HQ, an immediate check of the new remote, trashing Tranquility Home Grid, and an Overclock run on the advanced remote to win on turn 4.

Strong early steals, but the Runner then sat on 6 points for about 16 turns, repeatedly running Starlit Knight with no credits to break it and spending most clicks clearing the tags it took. It won only because the Corp also stalled.

It spent down to 0 credits on turn 1, which left it unable to steal the Architect Deployment Test it accessed. On T4 it ran R&D four times while the revealed Megaprix in a naked remote got scored, then lost Carmen to a Tithe facecheck and wasted second HQ runs through Vertigo, which blocks steals.

Steady R&D pressure through Paywall eventually won, but the economy stayed at 0-4 credits for most of the game. An Into the Depths run on the remote spent everything on Capacitor and then bounced off a 1-credit Paywall, letting Kingmaking score.

It hoarded 63 credits by clicking for credits nearly every turn and installed nothing after Boi-tata. Its few runs were ETR facechecks on Descent and Tree Line while the Corp scored five agendas from remotes.

Facechecking Saisentan against Personal Evolution cost the Runner its whole grip, and the economy never recovered. Late on, it clicked for credits with 10-14 in the pool while the Corp scored Lotus Haze and Regenesis from the same remote.

Good pressure on HQ and R&D won by turn 10, but against Personal Evolution it twice ended turns with 0 cards in grip, so any Corp score would have flatlined it. It also ran unknown remotes into Urtica Cipher with a tiny grip.

Persistent R&D runs through Virtual Service Agent won the game, but the Runner lived on 0-3 credits and carried tags against an NBN Corp with 40+ credits. It could not contest the Next Big Thing remote.
Won with good HQ, remote and R&D hits, but it lost Buzzsaw to a Ballista facecheck and kept running R&D into the recurring Descent ETR with no barrier breaker. It also let Divested Trust score.

For three turns it ran HQ with exactly 1 credit into Paywall, which drains 1 credit first and then ends the run unless paid, clicked a credit and repeated the same failure. Meanwhile the Corp installed and scored an agenda every other turn from Server 2, which the Runner never ran again.

It repeatedly ran a 3-card HQ seeing the same Moon Pool while the advanced Server 2 agenda was scored. Later it clicked for credits up to 21 while Fujii was advanced in Server 1 and scored for the win.
A coherent R&D lock through Anemone with Revolver won on turn 12. The minor issues were a thin economy, taking avoidable net damage on a small grip, and leaving the Server 2 scores uncontested.

It ran through unbroken Ansel 1.0, which bars stealing, four times a turn and re-ran Server 3 a dozen times only to decline Melies again. It never installed a breaker or contested Server 2, where the Corp scored four agendas.
Won 7-6 with a late HQ/R&D burst, but it let two SDS Drone Deployments score from a one-ice remote, choosing R&D runs over the advanced remote while holding 11 credits.
It made one run all game and otherwise clicked for credits to 62 with a full grip and only Odore installed, while the Corp scored five agendas unopposed.
Efficient aggressive play: early R&D steals, trashing Nico, and breaking Hagen to steal Melies from the advanced remote for a turn-8 win.

Stuck at 1 credit, it ran Funhouse and Vasilisa four times a turn and piled up dozens of tags, letting the Corp score Backroom Machinations twice. It never built an economy or installed breakers, and spent remaining clicks removing tags one at a time.
